- Provide a mobile-first, static React/TypeScript MVP for a browser-based quantum circuit playground with an in-browser state-vector simulator and a QPU AST compiler. 
- Offer starter examples and a simple UI to compose, run, step, reset, and measure circuits in the browser. 
- Enable easy deployment to GitHub Pages via an automated workflow.

bodies.pr:BPForbes/Bailey-Forbes-Flinstone#360:
Flintstone becomes the machine-readable source of truth for its own public project metadata. Every validated push to `main` now publishes **`dist/browser-lab/project-metadata.json`** as part of the *same atomic GitHub Pages deployment* the browser lab already uses, so **bailey-forbes.com** can consume it instead of maintaining duplicate static values.

Full contract: [`docs/project-metadata.md`](https://github.com/BPForbes/Bailey-Forbes-Flinstone/blob/claude/flintstone-project-metadata-isabru/docs/project-metadata.md)

---

## What metadata is generated

`schemaVersion: 1`, with common portfolio fields plus Flintstone-specific extensions:

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion`, `generatedAt`, `sourceCommit` | Contract version, generation instant, and the exact deployed build commit |
| `repository` | `owner`, `name`, `defaultBranch`, `url`, optional `description` |
| `languages[]` | `{ name, bytes, percentage }`, largest-to-smallest |
| `build` | `bootable`, `browserCompatible`, `bootSmokePassed`, `validationOutcome`, `architecture`, `artifactSha256`, `builtAt`, `blockers`, `browserValidation` subset |
| `lab` | `type: "browser-kernel"`, `architecture`, `executionModel: "emulated"`, `physicalHardwareDrivers: false`, `published` |
| `timeline[]` | Newest-first `pull_request` and `release` entries, each carrying a common `date` |

Common fields (`schemaVersion` / `generatedAt` / `sourceCommit` / `repository` / `languages` / `timeline`) are deliberately reusable so one portfolio consumer can serve several projects; `build` and `lab` are the project-specific extension.

## How GitHub Linguist is used

Linguist is the **authoritative classifier** — no file is manually classified because it belongs to the kernel or the browser lab. The generator reads `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`, which exposes exactly the Linguist-derived classification GitHub itself computes, including this repository's `.gitattributes` overrides and Linguist's vendored/generated handling. Running Linguist locally would only reproduce the same result with an extra Ruby toolchain, so the API is preferred.

No language whitelist exists. A newly introduced language appears with **zero generator changes**.

## How the GitHub REST API is used

| Data | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Repository metadata | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` |
| Language bytes | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages` |
| Merged PRs | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=closed&base=<default branch>` (paginated) |
| Authorship | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/commits` |
| Releases | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases` (paginated) |

Pagination stops on a short page and is bounded (`--max-pull-pages`, default 10). Transient 5xx/429 responses retry with backoff; an exhausted rate limit raises a clear error naming the reset time; non-JSON bodies and wrong JSON types are fatal. Nothing is swallowed.

## How percentages are calculated

```
percentage = round(bytes * 100 / total_bytes, 1)
```

Raw `bytes` are preserved so consumers can re-derive or re-round. Entries sort largest-to-smallest with a name tie-break for determinism. Nothing is hard-coded — a live run against this repository currently yields C 79.0%, Shell 5.3%, Assembly 4.0%, JavaScript 4.0%, Python 2.8%, and so on down to Linker Script.

## How PR timeline entries are selected

- **Merged only.** Open and closed-but-unmerged PRs never appear, and individual commits are not timeline entries.
- Newest-first with a deterministic tie-break, capped at `--max-timeline` (default 25).
- Real GitHub Releases become `release` entries. **Zero releases is supported** — entries are simply omitted, and nothing is fabricated from `version/*.ver`. The schema leaves room for releases to become stronger milestone markers later.

## How bot/agent-assisted and co-authored PRs are treated

A PR is **not** excluded because an agent created or pushed the branch. Cursor, Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Actions-assisted work stays eligible whenever a human is meaningfully associated. The generator inspects the PR author, the merge actor, the PR's commits, and standard `Co-authored-by:` trailers.

The **only** exclusion is a bot-authored *routine dependency chore* (`dependabot` / `renovate` / `build(deps): bump …`) with no human association at all.

```json
{ "author": "agent-or-primary-author", "coAuthors": ["BPForbes"] }
```

Bot identities appearing in commit metadata (e.g. `github-actions[bot]` version-lock commits) are treated as noise and skipped, while an explicit trailer is always honoured.

**No contributor email addresses are published.** A trailer's address is used only to resolve a public `…@users.noreply.github.com` login; anything else falls back to the display name. The validator walks every string in the finished document and refuses to write it if anything matches an email or credential pattern.

## How Flintstone build/validation state is incorporated

The generator **never computes compatibility**. It republishes what the existing pipeline already decided:

- `build.bootable` ← `dist/build-info.json` `bootable`
- `build.browserCompatible` ← `dist/build-info.json` `browserCompatible` (falling back to `v86Compatible` on schema-1 manifests)
- `build.bootSmokePassed` ← the workflow's QEMU boot-probe step output
- `build.browserValidation` ← compact subset of `dist/browser-validation.json`

`build-info.json` and `browser-validation.json` keep their existing responsibilities and are not duplicated. The generator **refuses to run** if the build manifest was produced from a different commit than the deployment's `GITHUB_SHA`, and `lab.published` can only be `true` when every promotion gate passed *and* this is the `main` push that deploys Pages. The lab is described honestly as an emulated demonstration — `executionModel: "emulated"`, `physicalHardwareDrivers: false`. No physical hardware-driver execution in the browser is claimed.

## Why browser-kernel-artifact.yml is the integration point

It already runs on PRs and `main` pushes, already builds and tests the kernel, validates the browser-kernel candidate, builds the Wasm lab, packages the static lab, stages `dist/browser-lab` as the Pages artifact, and deploys it. Generating metadata anywhere else would mean either a **second competing Pages deployment** or a **metadata-only publish that bypasses the promotion gate**. Neither is acceptable, so metadata generation is simply two more steps inside the existing job:

```
Merge into main
      ↓  kernel build + driver/VM/gate tests
      ↓  virtual boot probe (boot_smoke_passed)
      ↓  Wasm lab, browser boot, packaged-lab, iframe validation
      ↓  GitHub metadata generation      ← new
      ↓  verify metadata inside dist/browser-lab   ← new
      ↓  Stage Pages payload → Deploy GitHub Pages
```

No second Pages deployment, no workflow-generated commits, no recursive triggers. If generation fails, the step fails, the job fails, and **nothing is deployed** — metadata stays subordinate to the validation pipeline.

## Where project-metadata.json is placed

`dist/browser-lab/project-metadata.json`, written **after** `package_browser_lab_release.py` (which does a `rmtree` + `copytree`) and **before** `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, which uploads `dist/browser-lab`. A dedicated verification step asserts the file exists inside the payload, parses as JSON, carries `schemaVersion`, and has a `sourceCommit` equal to `github.sha`.

## Expected public endpoint

```
https://bpforbes.github.io/Bailey-Forbes-Flinstone/project-metadata.json
```

This is a Pages **project** site (no `CNAME` in `tools/browser-lab/`), which is why the path carries the `/Bailey-Forbes-Flinstone/` prefix — the same prefix `infra/cloudflare/flintstone-lab-worker.js` already uses as `BASE_PATH`, and the same base as the published lab URL documented in `docs/portfolio-iframe-integration.md`. The Cloudflare child Worker therefore also serves it at `https://flintstone.bailey-forbes.com/project-metadata.json`, and `project-metadata.json` joins `build-info.json` / `browser-validation.json` in the Worker's no-store set so consumers never read a stale revision.

⚠️ The live URL cannot be confirmed until this merges and `main` deploys — please spot-check it after the first `main` run rather than assuming it.

## How bailey-forbes.com consumes it

GitHub Pages serves `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so no proxy or token is needed and the portfolio must never make authenticated GitHub API calls from the browser:

```js
const metadata = await fetch(
  "https://bpforbes.github.io/Bailey-Forbes-Flinstone/project-metadata.json"
).then((response) => response.json());

const languages = metadata.languages
  .map((language) => `${language.name} ${language.percentage.toFixed(1)}%`);

const milestones = metadata.timeline;   // already newest-first
```

The portfolio should no longer maintain Flintstone language percentages, PR history, release history, source-commit information, or browser-validation state.

## Permissions added or changed

Top-level stays `contents: read`, and the `deploy` job keeps its separate `pages: write` / `id-token: write`. The `validate` job now declares:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read        # repository, languages, releases, commits
  pull-requests: read   # merged pull requests for the timeline
```

`pull-requests: read` is the only addition. Authentication uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` — **no PAT**, no token printed, no token in the published JSON.

## Tests and deployment validations performed

Run in this session:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/test_generate_project_metadata.py` (new, hermetic — fake transport, no network) | **PASS** |
| `make test-browser-kernel-gate` (fail-closed promotion gate) | **PASS** |
| `make test_drivers` (hardware-driver contracts) | **PASS** |
| All `make test-browser-lab` node/python unit contracts (`test_browser_lab`, `test_server_relay`, `test_server_relay_client`, `test_lab_relay_room`, `test_server_relay_clients_ws`, `test_browser_lab_process`, `test_flintstone_lab_worker`, `test_lab_dns`, `test_package_browser_lab_release`) | **PASS** |
| `tests/test_version_scripts.sh` | **91 passed, 0 failed** |
| All six `scripts/check_version_*.sh` policy checks | **ok** |
| `./scripts/gen_version_def.sh` produces **no** diff (header untouched, per CLAUDE.md) | **confirmed** |
| Workflow YAML parse + the new verification step executed against real generator output | **PASS** |
| Live generator run against the real GitHub API for this repository | **PASS** — 12 languages, correct timeline, `cursoragent` co-authorship preserved, `github-actions[bot]` filtered, no emails |

The new unit suite covers each verification item directly: dynamic percentages, a brand-new language needing no code change, merged-only timelines, closed-but-unmerged exclusion, agent-authored PRs with human co-authors staying eligible, bot-only dependency chores dropped, `users.noreply` login resolution, zero-release tolerance, `sourceCommit`/build-commit agreement, gate-faithful `bootable` / `browserCompatible` / `bootSmokePassed`, pagination, rate-limit and 5xx handling, and the atomic write that leaves a previously valid file intact when a malformed document is refused.

**Not verifiable from this environment** (egress to `bpforbes.github.io` is blocked here, and these only exist after a `main` deploy): the live public endpoint being reachable, the full end-to-end `main` Pages deployment, and the QEMU/Playwright stages of the browser workflow (`nasm`, `qemu-system-x86`, `emsdk`, and Playwright Chromium are unavailable here). Those run unchanged in CI on this PR — please confirm the endpoint after the first `main` deployment.

## Preserved behaviour
